chains.title: Risk allele A disrupts an AP-2alpha (TFAP2A) site in the MCS9.7-type IRF6 enhancer, lowering IRF6 in oral periderm
chains.element: EH38E2863563 / ENSR1_B3JM9C distal enhancer ~9.7 kb upstream of IRF6 (the MCS9.7-type enhancer)

links.claim: QBiC AP-2 group G030 predicts the alt G allele binds AP-2 proteins more strongly than ref A (effect +1.69; ref 78.9th vs alt 99.9th k-mer percentile), i.e. the cleft-risk A allele weakens an AP-2 site; within this specificity group TFAP2A is named not because it is the top-scoring model (it is the weakest member, z 11.94, and TFAP2A is listed only among the group's covered own/CIS-BP-mapped TFs) but because published EMSA and ChIP at this exact enhancer show the risk allele disrupts an AP-2alpha binding site; note no ENCODE TFAP2A ChIP peak covers the variant, which may reflect biosample coverage

The variant lies in an ENCODE distal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E2863563, DNase z 5.3, H3K27ac z 5.0, maxima across biosamples) and an Ensembl enhancer, and this element was independently identified by multispecies comparison as an IRF6 enhancer whose activity in mouse is craniofacial and limb

The element is 9.7 kb from the IRF6 TSS and IRF6 is the gene whose enhancer this was shown to be in reporter mice; L2G gives IRF6 up to 0.67 but UTP25 scores higher (0.75) and the cleft-specific set gives IRF6 only 0.16, so the gene assignment rests mainly on the published enhancer work plus IRF6's established cleft association (Open Targets 0.54, genetic_association 0.72)

Mouse expression analysis localises this enhancer's activity to craniofacial and limb structures, which is the only cell-type evidence available; the cited QTLs here are blood/monocyte TRAF3IP3 only, and there is no periderm eQTL or expression context in this case

Reduced AP-2alpha-driven IRF6 in periderm impairs epithelial differentiation and lip fusion, matching the A risk allele for orofacial clefts (p 2e-06, PIP only 0.05) and the common-variant risk attributed to rs642961 at this locus

predictions: Allele-specific EMSA/ChIP shows AP-2alpha binds the G allele and not (or much less) the A allele at this position
Luciferase/MPRA of this enhancer in keratinocyte or periderm-like cells gives lower activity for A
TFAP2A knockdown reduces enhancer activity and abolishes the allelic difference, whereas ETS or TEAD knockdown does not
Enhancer deletion or A/G base editing changes IRF6, not UTP25 or TRAF3IP3, in oral epithelial cells
falsified_if: EMSA/ChIP shows equal or A-preferential AP-2alpha binding at this site
Allelic reporter difference is absent or reversed in oral epithelial cells
TFAP2A depletion leaves the allelic difference intact

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs642961 itself; the cleft signal reflects a linked causal variant (e.g. the IRF6 promoter SNP) or another gene
predictions: Allele-specific reporter and TF occupancy assays show no difference between A and G at this position
Fine-mapping PIP stays low (orofacial clefts PIP 0.05) and the functional effect tracks a neighbouring variant such as the IRF6 promoter SNP rs12403599
Molecular QTL signal at this locus maps to TRAF3IP3 in blood rather than IRF6 in epithelium
The strongest association at this SNP (blood pressure) is unrelated to IRF6 enhancer function
falsified_if: Allele-specific enhancer activity or TF occupancy at rs642961 is demonstrated in epithelial cells
Base editing of this single position alters IRF6 expression or periderm phenotype

chains.element: EH38E2863563 distal enhancer upstream of IRF6

links.claim: The largest QBiC signal at this site is Ets group G003 (18/18 concordant models; ETV5 own model z 77.65, effect +1.32; ref 65.0th vs alt 99.2th percentile), with a second Ets group G345 (SPDEF own model, effect +1.62) also alt-preferring; ETV5 is named only as the group's best own model, and no expression or ChIP evidence here distinguishes it from ELF/EHF members covered by the same specificity
The predicted Ets gain lies within an active distal enhancer-like cCRE with high DNase/H3K27ac (biosample maxima)
IRF6 is 9.7 kb away and the element has reporter-validated IRF6 enhancer activity, though UTP25 has the higher best L2G (0.75 vs 0.67)
No cell-type evidence is cited for Ets factor expression in embryonic oral epithelium; the only available QTLs are blood/monocyte TRAF3IP3
Lower Ets-driven IRF6 on the A allele would reduce periderm IRF6 and raise cleft risk, direction-consistent with the A effect allele for orofacial clefts

predictions: Mutating only the Ets core, leaving the AP-2 core intact, abolishes the allelic reporter difference
ETS-family (ETV5/ELF3) ChIP shows allele-biased occupancy favouring G
Knockdown of an epithelial Ets factor, not TFAP2A, removes the allelic effect

Allelic effect persists after Ets-core mutagenesis
TFAP2A depletion alone removes the entire allelic difference

grades_v0.reason: E13 shows alt G binding AP-2 more (+1.69), a prediction only. The reason for picking TFAP2A is stated without support: TFAP2A is the lowest-scoring member (z 11.94) and E13/E04 contain no ChIP or literature for this IRF6 enhancer. The claim of ChIP and functional literature at this enhancer is not backed by any cited evidence. E04 does not bear on binding.
E01 and E03 place the variant in a dELS cCRE and Ensembl enhancer with high DNase and H3K27ac. The values are maxima across biosamples, so they are not tissue-specific.

IRF6 is 9.7 kb away and has L2G up to 0.67 (E05), but UTP25 has the best L2G (0.75) and shares the TSS region with the IRF6 neighbor. The L2G is for SBP sets and the cleft set gives only 0.16. There is no perturbation or tissue eQTL evidence linking this enhancer to IRF6.
E05 contains no periderm or epithelial data, only blood QTLs, and there is no expression context. Co-expression of IRF6 and AP-2 is asserted from memory.

E04 shows an orofacial clefts association (p 2e-06, effect allele A), which is direction-consistent. E06a says two SNPs near IRF6 explain most of the risk but does not name rs642961. The PIP is only 0.05, and the same SNP is strongly associated with blood pressure.

E08 and E09 show strong, concordant alt-preferring Ets predictions, but this is binding prediction only. ETV5 is the best-model default, and the claim itself says ELF3 may be the real binder with no reason or expression evidence for either.
E01 and E03 show the variant is in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE. The values are biosample maxima.
IRF6 is nearest, but UTP25 has a higher best L2G (0.75) than IRF6 (0.67). Calling IRF6 the highest-scoring target is inaccurate.
E05 has no epithelial data, and ETV5/ELF expression in embryonic epithelium is not cited.
The direction is consistent (A is low-Ets and the A allele is the cleft risk allele in E04), but only the association is cited, not any mechanism. The OFC association also has PIP 0.05.
E10 shows ref-preferring TEAD binding across all four TEADs, which is consistent with the claim but is only prediction. TEAD1 is chosen without any expression data.
E01 and E03 show an active dELS cCRE. TEAD activity in it is not shown.
IRF6 is close and has an L2G score, but UTP25 scores higher, and no perturbation data links the enhancer to IRF6.
No evidence is cited, and Hippo activity in craniofacial tissue is from memory.
The A-allele association (E04) is only compatible with the claim. The repressor role is speculative, as the claim also allows TEAD to activate, so the direction is not established.
E16 gives a ref-preferring SOX2 model, but the group members disagree on direction, and SOX2 is chosen with no expression data. Binding is prediction only.
E01 and E03 show an active enhancer cCRE.
IRF6 is nearest, but UTP25 has the higher best L2G. There is no functional link.
No evidence is cited, and SOX2 expression in oral epithelium is from memory.
The direction is only conditionally consistent (SOX2 would have to be a repressor), and E04 shows association only.

grades_final.reason: E19d cites EMSA and ChIP showing the risk allele disrupts an AP-2alpha site, and E19b says rs642961 abrogates one of four AP-2alpha sites. That is perturbation-level evidence for this variant and this TF. The QBiC G030 direction (alt binds more, so the risk A allele binds less) agrees. TFAP2A is weakest in G030, but it is chosen for a stated reason. E18 shows no ChIP peak, which does not contradict this.

E03 and E01 place the variant in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE (DNase z 5.3, H3K27ac z 5.0). E19c and E19d show it was identified as an IRF6 enhancer with craniofacial and limb activity in mouse. The cCRE values are biosample maxima, but the enhancer activity evidence is direct.

The evidence is proximity (9.7 kb), the published IRF6 enhancer identification (E19c, E19d), L2G of 0.67 for IRF6 and the Open Targets disease association. UTP25 has the higher best L2G (0.75), the cleft-specific L2G for IRF6 is only 0.16, and no CRISPR or eQTL evidence links this element to IRF6 expression. The chain acknowledges this.

E19d shows mouse enhancer activity in craniofacial and limb structures, which is consistent with a craniofacial role. It does not show activity in oral periderm specifically, and there is no human expression context or periderm eQTL. The chain admits it has only this evidence.

The orofacial cleft association (p 2e-06, effect allele A) agrees in direction with the AP-2 disruption on the risk allele. E19a and E06a attribute locus risk to rs642961 and nearby SNPs, but fine-mapping is weak (PIP 0.05). The IRF6-lowering and periderm mechanism is inferred, not shown.

The only evidence is a QBiC-SELEX prediction (G003 ETV5, G345 SPDEF) that the alt allele binds Ets proteins more strongly. This is a binding prediction alone. ETV5 is picked as the best own model with no reason to prefer it over other Ets members, and no ChIP or expression evidence supports it.
The variant is in an active enhancer-like cCRE (E01, E03). These are epigenomic context from biosample maxima only and say nothing about Ets occupancy at the site.

The evidence is proximity and the published IRF6 enhancer identification (E19c). The claim of reporter validation is partly supported, but UTP25 has the higher L2G and there is no direct evidence tying an Ets mechanism to IRF6.
The chain itself says no cell-type evidence for Ets expression in oral epithelium is cited. The cited E05 QTLs are blood/monocyte TRAF3IP3 and do not bear on the claim.

E04 shows the orofacial cleft association with effect allele A, which is direction-consistent with the lower-Ets A allele lowering IRF6. The Ets-IRF6 mechanism is unsupported, and the competing AP-2 literature is not addressed.

The only evidence is a QBiC-SELEX prediction that the ref A allele binds TEADs more (G031, z -40). TEAD1 is chosen as the best model without expression or ChIP support. Binding prediction alone is at best weak.
The enhancer-like cCRE context (E01, E03) is consistent with regulatory activity, but the chain itself notes that no cited data show TEAD occupancy.
The evidence is proximity and the published IRF6 enhancer (E19c). UTP25 has the higher L2G and nothing links TEAD to the regulation of IRF6.
No evidence IDs are cited and nothing supports TEAD/Hippo activity in craniofacial tissue at this element.

The A-allele cleft association (E04) is direction-consistent only if TEAD acts as a repressor, which the chain says is unproven. The link is speculative and the AP-2 evidence offers a better explanation.

In addition, a common variant (rs642961) in the IRF6 locus is found in 30% of the world's population and contributes risk for isolated orofacial clefting.
